name: Neurological Muscular Channelopathy Due to a Genetic Sodium Channel Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Sodium Channel Myotonia

criteria.description: Presence of clinical myotonia characterized by delayed muscle relaxation after voluntary contraction
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the SCN4A gene encoding the skeletal muscle sodium channel
Lack of significant muscle atrophy or weakness in early stages
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical myotonia, electromyographic myotonic discharges, and a pathogenic SCN4A mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other myotonic disorders and channelopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle stiffness exacerbated by cold exposure
searchTerms: increased muscle tone with cold exposure
weak muscles after episodes of stiffness
increased muscle bulk with normal strength
muscle hypertrophy without loss of power

occasional.symptomName: Episodic paralysis triggered by potassium imbalance
searchTerms: episodic paralysis caused by potassium imbalance

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia due to oropharyngeal muscle involvement

searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to sodium channel dysfunction
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems from sodium channel issues
cardiac arrhythmias due to channel dysfunction
abnormal heartbeats linked to sodium channels

laboratory: Serum potassium levels may fluctuate during episodic paralysis
Normal creatine kinase levels or mild elevation
imaging: Muscle MRI may show mild hypertrophy without fatty infiltration
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SCN4A gene identified by molecular genetic testing

distinguishingFeatures: Worsening of myotonia with repeated activity (paradoxical myotonia)
SCN4A mutations but different clinical pattern
Episodes of flaccid paralysis with elevated serum potassium
Triggers include rest after exercise and potassium-rich foods

redFlags: Progressive respiratory muscle weakness causing respiratory failure
Sudden onset of severe paralysis with cardiac arrhythmia
Rapidly worsening muscle weakness inconsistent with typical myotonia
